title: Athiradi Crosses ₹51 Crore Worldwide — Why Malayalam Cinema's Latest Hit Is NRI Gold
excerpt: Tovino Thomas and Basil Joseph's campus action-comedy is smashing records overseas, and Drishyam 3 hasn't even landed yet.
body:
Malayalam cinema doesn't wait for permission to dominate — it just does. And right now, Athiradi is the latest proof.

In just six days since its May 14 release, the Tovino Thomas and Basil Joseph-led action-comedy has crossed ₹51.12 crore at the worldwide box office, securing its place as the fourth-highest-grossing Malayalam film of 2026. But here's the number that should make every NRI Malayali smile: ₹21.75 crore from overseas markets alone.

The Plot: Campus Chaos Meets Musical Mayhem

Directed by Arun Anirudhan, Athiradi follows Samkutty (Basil Joseph), an engineering student whose mission to revive his college's banned "Arohan" festival spirals into absolute chaos when Sreekuttan Vellayani (Tovino Thomas) — a former local goon turned aspiring musician — gets dragged into the mess. What starts as campus comedy slowly morphs into a high-energy showdown, complete with misunderstandings, a kidnapped chief guest, and the kind of escalating ridiculousness that only Malayalam cinema can pull off with a straight face.

Vineeth Sreenivasan, Riya Shibu, and Zarin Shihab round out a solid ensemble cast. The music by Vishnu Vijay has been widely praised, and BookMyShow audiences have given the film an impressive 8.3/10 rating.

The Numbers That Matter

Athiradi's box office trajectory tells a story of genuine audience love:

  • Opening weekend (Kerala): ₹20.25 crore
  • India net (6 days): ₹25.32 crore
  • Overseas gross: ₹21.75 crore
  • Worldwide total: ₹51.12 crore and climbing

The overseas number is particularly striking. Screens across the Gulf, the US, UK, Canada, and Australia have been packed with NRI Malayali families turning out for what's essentially a nostalgia-laced campus entertainer — the kind of film that reminds diaspora audiences of college fests, local rivalries, and the beautiful chaos of Kerala life.

Why NRIs Are Driving This Film's Global Run

Malayalam cinema has a unique relationship with its diaspora. Unlike Bollywood's scatter-shot global appeal, Malayalam films consistently punch above their weight overseas because NRI Malayalis are among the most loyal cinema-going communities in the world. Athiradi taps into that perfectly — it's a film about homecoming, about the energy of youth, and about the kind of community bonds that NRIs miss the most.

The fact that Basil Joseph (who also co-produced the film) and Tovino Thomas are both bonafide stars in the NRI circuit helps enormously. Both actors have massive followings in Gulf countries and North America, and screenings have been selling out in cities like Houston, Toronto, and Sydney.

The Drishyam 3 Test

The real challenge starts now. Mohanlal's Drishyam 3 drops on May 21 — just two days away — and it's the biggest Malayalam release of the year with ₹25 crore already locked in pre-sales. Athiradi needs to hold screens and sustain momentum against a cultural juggernaut.

But here's the thing: the two films aren't competing for the same audience emotion. Drishyam 3 is a psychological thriller sequel riding decades of legacy. Athiradi is pure, unapologetic fun. There's room for both in the diaspora's weekend plans.

The Verdict

Athiradi won't rewrite the grammar of Malayalam cinema, and critics have noted that its second half dips into tonal confusion. But it doesn't need to be revolutionary — it needs to be entertaining, and it absolutely is. Tovino Thomas brings charisma in waves, Basil Joseph is a riot, and the film's energy is infectious enough to fill theaters worldwide.

If you're an NRI Malayali who hasn't caught it yet, check your nearest screening. If you're not Malayali — give it a shot anyway. Some things don't need subtitles to feel universal.

Now playing in cinemas worldwide | Director: Arun Anirudhan | Cast: Tovino Thomas, Basil Joseph, Vineeth Sreenivasan | Music: Vishnu Vijay | Rating: 3.5/5
